title: Import & Export Syntax
definition: The precise syntax used to expose and consume modules in TypeScript, including named exports, default exports, and re-exporting.
simpleExplanation: Named exports are like a grocery store aisle: you pick exactly which specific items you want from the shelf using `{ }`. Default exports are like a subscription box: the file hands you one main item, and you can name the box whatever you want when you receive it.
realWorldExample: A `utils.ts` file exports 10 different helper functions using named exports. In `app.ts`, you only `import { formatDate }` so you don't load the other 9 into memory.

basic: What is the difference between Named and Default exports?
intermediate: Can a file have both a default export and named exports?
advanced: What is a Barrel File (`export * from`)?

answers.question: Can a file have both?
answers.answer: Yes. A file can have an infinite number of Named exports, and exactly ONE Default export.

answers.question: What is a Barrel File?
answers.answer: An `index.ts` file that imports from many files in a folder and immediately re-exports them. It allows consumers to import from the folder directly `import { User, Post } from './models'` instead of `import { User } from './models/user'; import { Post } from './models/post';`.
